q: Håstad's switching lemma proves that parity (XOR) is not in AC⁰ (constant-depth polynomial-size circuits) because:
opts: A random restriction of variables leaves parity hard: any depth-d AC⁰ circuit for parity requires size exp(Ω(n^{1/(d-1)}))
Parity is in P but not in NC¹
exp: Håstad (1987): the switching lemma shows that after a random restriction, DNFs of width w simplify to small decision trees. Applied to any AC⁰ circuit computing parity, each gate simplifies, but the lower-level logic proves parity requires exponential AC⁰ size (grows with depth).
